title: Polity Lec 4
summary: Parliament = President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha (Art. 79); Rajya Sabha Art. 80 (Fourth Schedule), Lok Sabha Art. 81; Part V covers Articles 52-151 in 5 chapters.
Rajya Sabha: maximum 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated); nomination borrowed from Ireland, election method from South Africa; RED = Ireland: Rajya Sabha nomination, Election of President, DPSP.

First sitting of Parliament on 13 May 1952; minimum age 25 years for Lok Sabha and 30 years for Rajya Sabha (Art. 84); duration Art. 83; summoning/prorogation/dissolution Art. 85; gap between two sessions cannot exceed 6 months.

Anti-defection law: 52nd Amendment 1985, Tenth Schedule; an independent member joining any party at any time is disqualified, a nominated member joining after 6 months is disqualified; disqualification Art. 102, decision Art. 103 (President); Speaker's decision on defection is subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan, 1992).

Special Address by the President (Motion of Thanks) Art. 87; delivered at the first session after a general election and the first session of each year; drafted by the Council of Ministers; if the motion fails, the government falls.

Quorum one-tenth (Art. 100(3)); Art. 99 oath (Pro-tem Speaker), 94 resignation/removal of Speaker, 96 Speaker not to preside while removal resolution is pending, 104 penalty Rs 500 per day, 105 privileges (no civil proceedings 40 days before and after a session).

Art. 107 ordinary bills, 108 joint sitting (from Australia; ordinary bills only; held thrice: 1961 Dowry, 1978 Banking, 2002 POTA), 109 money bill procedure, 110 definition, 111 assent/veto, 112 Budget, 114 Appropriation, 115 supplementary grants, 117 Finance Bill.

Veto: absolute, suspensive and pocket (India); qualified veto exists in the USA. No suspensive veto on money bills; no veto on Constitutional Amendment Bills (24th Amendment 1971). Money bill: President's recommendation, introduced only in Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha has 14 days, Speaker certifies (Aadhaar case).

Five cases in which Parliament legislates on the State List: Art. 249 (Rajya Sabha special majority), 250 (National Emergency), 252 (request of two or more states), 253 (international treaties), 356 (President's Rule); Art. 254 deals with repugnancy.

Financial committees: Public Accounts (22 members, 1921, 15+7), Estimates (30 members, all from Lok Sabha, 1950, John Mathai), Public Undertakings (22, Krishna Menon Committee); term 1 year; ministers cannot be members.
Delimitation Commission Art. 82; Acts of 1952, 1962, 1972, 2002; freeze till 2000 by 42nd Amendment and till 2026 by 84th; 87th Amendment allowed internal readjustment on the 2001 Census.

Reservation: Art. 330/332 SC-ST in Lok Sabha/Assemblies (extended 10 years by 104th Amendment), 331/333 Anglo-Indian nomination abolished; 106th Amendment 33% reservation for women; Panchayats 243D, Municipalities 243T; Indra Sawhney 1992, Mandal Commission 1979.

Part VI has 6 chapters, Articles 152-237; add 89 to Parliament's articles to get the State article (81->170, 85->174, 87->176, 93->182, 99->188, 102->191); from 112 onward add 90 (112->202, 123->213); no joint sitting in states.

Legislative Council: 6 states (UP, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana), Art. 169 creation/abolition, 171 composition (maximum one-third of Assembly, minimum 40; raised from 1/4 to 1/3 by 7th Amendment); 1/3 by MLAs, 1/3 by local bodies, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, 1/6 nominated by Governor.
UTs with Legislative Assemblies: Delhi (69th Amendment, Art. 239AA), Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir; ordinances Art. 123/213 (D.C. Wadhwa case); Budget laid in the name of the President/Governor.

mcqs.q: From which country has India adopted the parliamentary system of government, also called the Westminster model?
mcqs.e: Westminster is the seat of the British Parliament, hence the name Westminster model.

mcqs.q: Which is the supreme forum for discussion and debate on public issues and national policy?
mcqs.e: The Supreme Court is a judicial body; Parliament is the supreme forum for policy debate.

mcqs.q: From which country has India borrowed the concept of Judicial Review?
mcqs.e: Judicial Review is borrowed from the USA.

mcqs.q: In the USA, the principle of judicial review first emerged from which case?
mcqs.e: Judicial review was established in Marbury v. Madison (1803).

mcqs.q: Which Part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union Parliament?
mcqs.e: Part V deals with the Union, Part VI with the States and Part VIII with Union Territories.

mcqs.q: Why is Part VII of the Constitution not available?
o: It was repealed by the 7th Amendment
It was deleted by the 42nd Amendment
It was deleted by the 44th Amendment
mcqs.e: Part VII (Part B States) was repealed by the 7th Amendment (1956).

mcqs.q: How many chapters are there in Part V of the Constitution?
mcqs.e: Part V has 5 chapters; Part VI has 6.

mcqs.q: What is the range of Articles in Part V?
mcqs.e: Part V: Articles 52-151.

mcqs.q: Chapter I of Part V (The Union Executive) covers which Articles?
mcqs.e: Chapter I, The Executive: Articles 52-78.

mcqs.q: Parliament is described in which Articles of Part V?
mcqs.e: Chapter II, Parliament: Articles 79-122.

mcqs.q: The President's power to promulgate ordinances is given in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 123 covers the President's ordinances and Article 213 the Governor's.

mcqs.q: The Supreme Court is described in which Articles?
mcqs.e: Chapter IV, Union Judiciary: Articles 124-147.

mcqs.q: Which Articles deal with the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)?
mcqs.e: Chapter V, CAG: Articles 148-151.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Union Executive?
mcqs.e: Union Executive: President, Vice-President, PM and Council of Ministers, Attorney General.

mcqs.q: Who takes the place of the Attorney General in the State Executive?
mcqs.e: States have an Advocate General.

mcqs.q: Which post in the State Executive is equivalent to the Vice-President?
mcqs.e: There is no constitutional post like a Vice-Governor in the states.

mcqs.q: Which Article describes the constitution of the Indian Parliament?
mcqs.e: Article 79: Parliament = President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.q: Who constitute the Indian Parliament?
o: Only Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
Prime Minister, Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha
President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
mcqs.e: No bill becomes law without the President's assent, so the President is an integral part of Parliament.

mcqs.q: The composition of the Rajya Sabha is described in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 80 covers the Rajya Sabha and Article 81 the Lok Sabha.

mcqs.q: The composition of the Lok Sabha is given in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 81 lays down the composition of the Lok Sabha.

mcqs.q: By what other name is the Lok Sabha known?
mcqs.e: Lok Sabha = House of the People, Lower House, First Chamber.

mcqs.q: By which name is the Rajya Sabha NOT known?
mcqs.e: Rajya Sabha: Council of States, Permanent House, House of Elders, Federal Chamber, Second Chamber.

mcqs.q: What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha?
mcqs.e: Maximum 250: 238 elected + 12 nominated.

mcqs.q: How many members does the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
mcqs.e: 12 members are nominated from art, literature, science and social service.

mcqs.q: From which fields does the President nominate members to the Rajya Sabha?
o: Literature, science, art and social service
mcqs.e: Mnemonic LASS: Literature, Art, Science, Social service.

mcqs.q: Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha is given in which Schedule?
mcqs.e: The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats.

mcqs.q: What is the main basis for allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha?
mcqs.e: Representation is based on population, so UP has the most seats (31).

mcqs.q: Which Union Territories are represented in the Rajya Sabha (as per the lecture)?
o: Delhi and Puducherry (along with Jammu and Kashmir)
mcqs.e: Only UTs with legislatures (Delhi, Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir) are represented in the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.q: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by which system?
o: Proportional representation by single transferable vote
mcqs.e: The election is indirect; elected MLAs of the states cast the votes.

mcqs.q: When was the first sitting of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha held?
mcqs.e: First sitting on 13 May 1952; Rajya Sabha constituted on 3 April and Lok Sabha on 17 April 1952.

mcqs.q: The provision of nomination to the Rajya Sabha has been borrowed from which country?
mcqs.e: From Ireland (RED): Rajya Sabha nomination, Election of President, DPSP.

mcqs.q: The method of election of Rajya Sabha members was borrowed from which country?
mcqs.e: From South Africa: amendment procedure (Art. 368) and election of Rajya Sabha members.

mcqs.q: The procedure for amendment of the Constitution (Article 368) is borrowed from which country?
mcqs.e: South Africa: amendment procedure and election of Rajya Sabha members.

mcqs.q: From which country did India borrow the method of election of the President and the DPSP?
mcqs.e: From Ireland (RED): Rajya Sabha nomination, Election of President, DPSP.

mcqs.q: The First Schedule deals with what?
o: Names and territories of States and Union Territories
mcqs.e: First Schedule: names and territories of States and UTs.

mcqs.q: What is described in the Second Schedule?
o: Emoluments and allowances of constitutional functionaries
mcqs.e: Second Schedule: emoluments of the President, Governors, Speaker, judges, etc.

mcqs.q: What is contained in the Third Schedule?
o: Forms of oaths/affirmations of various functionaries
mcqs.e: Third Schedule: forms of oaths and affirmations.

mcqs.q: The Sixth Schedule provides for administration of tribal areas in which states?
mcqs.e: The Fifth Schedule covers tribal areas of other states.

mcqs.q: Which Schedule of the Citizenship Act, 1955 lays down the qualifications for citizenship by naturalisation?
mcqs.e: Qualifications for naturalisation (Section 6) are in the Third Schedule; the oath is in the Second Schedule.

mcqs.q: Why do changes in the First and Fourth Schedules not require a constitutional amendment under Art. 368?
o: Because Rajya Sabha's consent is not required
Because the President issues a notification
Under Article 4, such changes are made by simple majority
mcqs.e: Article 4: laws under Articles 2 and 3 are not deemed amendments under Art. 368.

mcqs.q: Reservation of seats for SCs/STs in the Lok Sabha is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 330 for the Lok Sabha and Art. 332 for State Assemblies.

mcqs.q: Reservation of seats for SCs/STs in State Legislative Assemblies is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 332 provides SC/ST reservation in State Assemblies.

mcqs.q: What changed in the Lok Sabha/State Assemblies by the 104th Constitutional Amendment?
o: Anglo-Indian nomination ended and SC/ST reservation extended by 10 years
mcqs.e: Anglo-Indian nominations under Art. 331 and 333 were discontinued.

mcqs.q: Under Article 331, how many members of the Anglo-Indian community could the President nominate to the Lok Sabha?
mcqs.e: The President could nominate 2; this was ended by the 104th Amendment.

mcqs.q: Under Article 333, who nominated an Anglo-Indian member to the State Assembly?
mcqs.e: The Governor could nominate 1 Anglo-Indian; now discontinued.

mcqs.q: Reservation for SCs/STs and women in Panchayats is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: 243D: reservation, including one-third seats for women.

mcqs.q: Reservation in Municipalities is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: 243D for Panchayats, 243T for Municipalities.

mcqs.q: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats are given in which Article?
mcqs.e: The corresponding Article for Municipalities is 243W.

mcqs.q: Audit of accounts of Panchayats is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: The corresponding Article for Municipalities is 243Z.

mcqs.q: Wards Committees of Municipalities are provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: 243S: Wards Committees.

mcqs.q: The duration of Panchayats (5 years) is given in which Article?
mcqs.e: Duration of Municipalities is in Article 243U.

mcqs.q: Duration of Municipalities is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: 243U: duration of Municipalities (5 years).

mcqs.q: The State Finance Commission for Panchayats is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: For Municipalities, Article 243Y refers to the State Finance Commission.

mcqs.q: When was the Mandal Commission (Second Backward Classes Commission) set up?
mcqs.e: Set up in 1979; its recommendations were implemented by the V.P. Singh government in 1990.

mcqs.q: The Mandal Commission's recommendations were implemented during the tenure of which Prime Minister?
mcqs.e: The V.P. Singh government implemented them in 1990.

mcqs.q: The Indra Sawhney case (Mandal case) belongs to which year?
mcqs.e: The Supreme Court upheld OBC reservation but disallowed reservation in promotions.

mcqs.q: What did the Supreme Court hold in the Indra Sawhney case?
o: OBC reservation is valid but not in promotions
mcqs.e: Later the 77th Amendment inserted Art. 16(4A) allowing reservation in promotion.

mcqs.q: Article 16(4A) provides reservation for whom?
mcqs.e: Inserted by the 77th Amendment; reservation in promotion.

mcqs.q: Clause (6) of Article 15 relates to reservation for whom?
mcqs.e: Inserted by the 103rd Amendment; Art. 16(6) has a similar provision.

mcqs.q: Article 15(1) prohibits the State from discriminating on which grounds?
o: Religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth
mcqs.e: The word 'only' is key; discrimination on other grounds may be permissible.

mcqs.q: Which clause of Article 15 prohibits restrictions on access to public places?
mcqs.e: Clause 3: special provisions for women and children; Clause 4: socially and educationally backward classes.

mcqs.q: Clause (5) of Article 15 relates to what?
o: Special provisions for backward classes in educational institutions
mcqs.e: Clause 5: reservation in educational institutions, including private ones.

mcqs.q: Article 16 deals with what?
o: Equality of opportunity in public employment
mcqs.e: Under Art. 16(3), Parliament may prescribe residence requirements.

mcqs.q: Reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies has been provided by which amendment?
mcqs.e: One-third seats in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, effective after the next census-based delimitation, for 15 years.

mcqs.q: What percentage of seats is reserved for women under the 106th Amendment?
mcqs.e: Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam; reservation for 15 years.

mcqs.q: What is the minimum age for membership of the Lok Sabha?
mcqs.e: Article 84: Lok Sabha 25 years, Rajya Sabha 30 years.

mcqs.q: What is the minimum age for membership of the Rajya Sabha?
mcqs.e: Hence the Rajya Sabha is called the House of Elders.

mcqs.q: Qualifications for membership of Parliament are given in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 83 duration, 84 qualifications, 85 summoning of sessions.

mcqs.q: The anti-defection law was added by which amendment?
mcqs.e: It added the Tenth Schedule.

mcqs.q: Which Schedule of the Constitution deals with disqualification on grounds of defection?
mcqs.e: Tenth Schedule: anti-defection law.

mcqs.q: Under the anti-defection law, when is an independent MP disqualified for joining a political party?
o: If he joins at any time
mcqs.e: The six-month window applies only to nominated members.

mcqs.q: When is a nominated member disqualified for joining a political party?
mcqs.e: Joining within 6 months of taking the seat does not attract disqualification.

mcqs.q: What does a party 'Whip' mean?
o: Party functionary who directs members on voting in the House
mcqs.e: Literally a whip is a lash, but in practice it is a party official.

mcqs.q: Who generally decides the disqualification of a member on grounds of defection?
mcqs.e: The decision is subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu, 1992).

mcqs.q: In which case was it held that the Speaker's decision on defection is subject to judicial review?
mcqs.e: Decided in 1992.

mcqs.q: The Eleventh Schedule relates to what?
mcqs.e: Added by the 73rd Amendment (1992); came into force on 24 April 1993.

mcqs.q: How many functional subjects are there in the Twelfth Schedule?
mcqs.e: Added by the 74th Amendment; relates to Municipalities.

mcqs.q: The Eleventh Schedule was added by which amendment?
mcqs.e: Passed in 1992 and came into force in 1993.

mcqs.q: The Ninth Schedule relates to what?
mcqs.e: Land reform laws are placed in the Ninth Schedule.

mcqs.q: Disqualification of an MP is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 102 disqualifications; Art. 101 vacation of seats.

mcqs.q: Who has the final say on questions of disqualification of an MP (Art. 103)?
o: President (on the opinion of the Election Commission)
mcqs.e: The President decides after obtaining the Election Commission's opinion.

mcqs.q: Which section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with disqualification on conviction?
mcqs.e: Conviction with 2 or more years' sentence disqualifies, plus 6 years after release.

mcqs.q: Under the RPA 1951, what sentence disqualifies an MP/MLA?
mcqs.e: Disqualification continues for 6 years after release.

mcqs.q: The President's special address is followed by which motion in the House?
mcqs.e: The Constitution calls it the 'Special Address by the President'.

mcqs.q: The President's special address is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 86 right to address/send messages; Art. 87 special address.

mcqs.q: When does the President address both Houses assembled together?
o: At the first session after a general election and the first session of each year
mcqs.e: The address is drafted by the government (Council of Ministers).

mcqs.q: Who prepares the President's address?
mcqs.e: The President reads it as drafted.

mcqs.q: What happens if the Motion of Thanks is defeated in the Lok Sabha?
mcqs.e: It means the government has lost its majority.

mcqs.q: The duration of the Lok Sabha is given in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 83: Rajya Sabha is permanent, Lok Sabha has 5 years.

mcqs.q: What is the term of a Rajya Sabha member?
mcqs.e: One-third of members retire every two years.

mcqs.q: What proportion of Rajya Sabha members retire every 2 years?
mcqs.e: Hence the Rajya Sabha is never dissolved.

mcqs.q: The power to summon and prorogue Parliament and dissolve the Lok Sabha is given in which Article?
mcqs.e: The President exercises these on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

mcqs.q: How many sessions of Parliament are usually held in a year?
mcqs.e: Budget, Monsoon and Winter; at least two sittings a year are mandatory.

mcqs.q: What is the maximum permissible gap between two sessions of Parliament?
mcqs.e: The gap between two sessions cannot exceed 6 months.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest session of Parliament?
mcqs.e: The Budget session runs from February to late April; the Winter session is the shortest.

mcqs.q: Which is the shortest session of Parliament?
mcqs.e: The Winter session is held in November-December.

mcqs.q: Who has the power to dissolve a House?
mcqs.e: The Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved.

mcqs.q: Who has the power to adjourn a sitting of the House?
mcqs.e: The Speaker in the Lok Sabha and the Chairman in the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
mcqs.e: Articles 64 and 89; he is not a member of either House.

mcqs.q: What is the quorum of a House?
mcqs.e: Article 100(3); without quorum the presiding officer may adjourn the House.

mcqs.q: The quorum of a House is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 100(1) relates to voting in the House.

mcqs.q: What does 'Adjournment sine die' mean?
o: Adjourning the House without fixing a date for the next sitting
mcqs.e: No date is fixed for the next sitting.

mcqs.q: Which judicial doctrine holds that Parliament can amend the Constitution without destroying its basic structure?
mcqs.e: It emerged from the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

mcqs.q: The Doctrine of Severability is related to which Article?
mcqs.e: Only the inconsistent part of a law is struck down, not the entire law.

mcqs.q: The Doctrine of Eclipse relates to what?
mcqs.e: Pre-constitutional laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights become dormant (eclipsed).

mcqs.q: Which doctrine allows laws implementing DPSP to be read in harmony with Fundamental Rights?
mcqs.e: Doctrine of Harmonious Construction.

mcqs.q: Parliament's power to create/abolish Legislative Councils is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: No Art. 368 amendment is needed; Parliament acts by ordinary law.

mcqs.q: Vacation of seats of Members of Parliament is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 99 oath, 100 voting/quorum, 101 vacation, 102 disqualification, 103 decision, 104 penalty.

mcqs.q: Oath/affirmation of Members of Parliament is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: The Pro-tem Speaker administers the oath to newly elected members.

mcqs.q: Who administers the oath to members of a new Lok Sabha?
mcqs.e: The Pro-tem Speaker is temporary and appointed by the President.

mcqs.q: Who appoints the Pro-tem Speaker?
mcqs.e: The President also administers the oath to the Pro-tem Speaker.

mcqs.q: Who was the Pro-tem Speaker of the 18th Lok Sabha?
mcqs.e: He administered oaths; the House then elected Om Birla as Speaker.

mcqs.q: Election of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 89-92 Rajya Sabha officers, 93-96 Lok Sabha officers.

mcqs.q: What does Article 96 provide?
o: Speaker/Deputy Speaker not to preside while a resolution for his removal is under consideration
mcqs.e: Art. 94 covers vacation, resignation and removal.

mcqs.q: Resignation, vacation and removal of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 97 covers salaries of the Chairman, Deputy Chairman, Speaker and Deputy Speaker.

mcqs.q: Salaries and allowances of the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman and Deputy Chairman are provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 98 deals with the Secretariat of Parliament.

mcqs.q: To whom does the Speaker of the Lok Sabha submit his resignation?
mcqs.e: The Deputy Speaker resigns to the Speaker.

mcqs.q: Who fixes the date of election of the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
mcqs.e: The date of the Speaker's election is fixed by the President.

mcqs.q: Since when has the post of Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha been vacant?
mcqs.e: It stayed vacant through the 17th Lok Sabha (2019-24) and remains so.

mcqs.q: The joint sitting is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 107 ordinary bills, 109 money bill procedure, 110 definition.

mcqs.q: The concept of a joint sitting is borrowed from which country's constitution?
mcqs.e: From Australia: joint sitting, Concurrent List, freedom of trade and commerce.

mcqs.q: The Concurrent List and freedom of trade and commerce were borrowed from which country?
mcqs.e: The joint sitting was also borrowed from Australia.

mcqs.q: A joint sitting of Parliament can be called for which bill?
mcqs.e: There is no joint sitting for money bills or Constitutional Amendment Bills.

mcqs.q: Who presides over a joint sitting?
mcqs.e: In his absence the Deputy Speaker, then the Deputy Chairman; never the Chairman.

mcqs.q: Why does the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Vice-President) not preside over a joint sitting?
o: He is from the Lok Sabha
He is a member of the Rajya Sabha
He is not a member of either House
mcqs.e: The Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman but not a member.

mcqs.q: A joint sitting is governed by whose rules?
mcqs.e: Decisions are taken by simple majority.

mcqs.q: How is a bill passed in a joint sitting?
o: By simple majority of members present and voting
mcqs.e: The Lok Sabha dominates owing to its larger numbers.

mcqs.q: How many times has a joint sitting been held so far?
mcqs.e: Dowry Prohibition Bill 1961, Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill 1978, POTA 2002.

mcqs.q: On which of the following bills was a joint sitting NOT held?
mcqs.e: Joint sittings were held in 1961, 1978 and 2002.

mcqs.q: When was a joint sitting held to pass the POTA (Prevention of Terrorism) Bill?
mcqs.e: Dowry Prohibition (1961), Banking Service Commission (1978), POTA (2002).

mcqs.q: Ordinary bills are provided for in which Article?
mcqs.e: An ordinary bill goes through three readings: first, second and third.

mcqs.q: When does a deadlock arise over an ordinary bill?
o: The first House does not pass it in 3 months
The other House rejects the bill or takes no action for 6 months
Rajya Sabha does not return it in 14 days
mcqs.e: A joint sitting under Art. 108 is called to resolve the deadlock.

mcqs.q: Every ordinary bill passes through how many readings?
mcqs.e: First reading: introduction; second: discussion/amendments; third: voting.

mcqs.q: The President's assent to bills (veto) is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: The President may give assent, withhold it, or return the bill.

mcqs.q: Which veto does the Indian President NOT possess?
mcqs.e: The qualified veto is available to the US President.

mcqs.q: What happens under an absolute veto?
o: The President withholds assent and the bill ends
mcqs.e: Under suspensive veto the bill is returned; under pocket veto no response is given.

mcqs.q: What does pocket veto mean?
o: The President takes no decision on the bill
mcqs.e: The Constitution prescribes no time limit for the President's decision.

mcqs.q: On which bill can the President NOT exercise the suspensive veto?
mcqs.e: A money bill is introduced only with the President's prior recommendation.

mcqs.q: Which amendment made it clear that the President has no veto over Constitutional Amendment Bills?
mcqs.e: The President is bound to give assent.

mcqs.q: A bill to change the names, boundaries or areas of states (Art. 3) is introduced in Parliament on whose prior recommendation?
mcqs.e: The President refers it to the concerned State Legislature for its views.

mcqs.q: Which amendment empowered the President to fix a time limit for the State Legislature's views on an Art. 3 bill?
mcqs.e: The President can specify the period for the State Legislature to respond.

mcqs.q: Which type of bill can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only on the President's prior recommendation?
mcqs.e: Art. 3 bills also need the President's recommendation.

mcqs.q: The procedure for money bills is given in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 110 defines a money bill.

mcqs.q: A money bill is defined in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 110 contains the definition of a money bill.

mcqs.q: In which House can a money bill be introduced?
mcqs.e: The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations.

mcqs.q: Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return a money bill?
mcqs.e: Otherwise it is deemed passed in the form passed by the Lok Sabha.

mcqs.q: Who certifies that a bill is a money bill?
mcqs.e: His decision is final under Art. 110(3), though courts examined it in the Aadhaar case.

mcqs.q: Which case dealt with the controversy over passing the Aadhaar Act as a money bill?
mcqs.e: Puttaswamy is also known for the right to privacy.

mcqs.q: What power does the Rajya Sabha have over a money bill?
mcqs.e: The Lok Sabha is not bound to accept its recommendations.

mcqs.q: Who introduces a Private Member's Bill?
o: An MP who is not a minister
mcqs.e: It is a type of ordinary bill.

mcqs.q: The Annual Financial Statement (Budget) is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: The word 'Budget' does not appear in the Constitution.

mcqs.q: In whose name is the Union Budget laid before Parliament?
mcqs.e: The Finance Minister presents it on behalf of the President.

mcqs.q: Which statement about discussion and voting on the Budget is correct?
o: Discussion only in the Lok Sabha
Discussion in both Houses, voting only in the Lok Sabha
Voting only in the Rajya Sabha
mcqs.e: Demands for grants are voted only in the Lok Sabha.

mcqs.q: What is India's financial year?
mcqs.e: The Annual Financial Statement covers this period.

mcqs.q: The Appropriation Bill is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Without it the government cannot withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund.

mcqs.q: The Consolidated Fund of India is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 267 deals with the Contingency Fund.

mcqs.q: Supplementary, additional and excess grants are provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: These grants are sought when needs arise after the Budget.

mcqs.q: The Finance Bill is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: The Finance Bill relates to taxation proposals.

mcqs.q: Under Article 104, what is the penalty per day for sitting or voting in the House without oath or when disqualified?
mcqs.e: The penalty of Rs 500 is levied for each day.

mcqs.q: Privileges and immunities of Members of Parliament are given in which Article?
mcqs.e: An MP is not liable in any court for anything said or any vote given in the House.

mcqs.q: For how many days before and after a session can no civil proceedings be brought against an MP?
mcqs.e: This immunity does not extend to criminal cases.

mcqs.q: How many months' prior notice is required for a civil suit against the President/Governor during the term of office?
mcqs.e: No criminal proceedings can be instituted against them during their term.

mcqs.q: Under Article 246, who has exclusive power to make laws on the Union List?
mcqs.e: Both can legislate on the Concurrent List; in conflict, Parliament's law prevails.

mcqs.q: In case of conflict on a Concurrent List subject, when can a state law prevail?
o: When the bill reserved by the Governor receives the President's assent
mcqs.e: Art. 254(2); Parliament can still override it later.

mcqs.q: Reservation of a bill by the Governor for the President's consideration is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 200 deals with the Governor's assent to bills.

mcqs.q: The 'Doctrine of Repugnancy' regarding conflict between Union and State laws is in which Article?
mcqs.e: It relates to Concurrent List subjects.

mcqs.q: What did the Supreme Court hold in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)?
o: The President can change the basic structure
Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot alter its basic structure
mcqs.e: The term 'basic structure' does not appear in the Constitution.

mcqs.q: In how many situations can Parliament legislate on a State List subject (as per the lecture)?
Which Article allows the Rajya Sabha to empower Parliament to legislate on the State List in the national interest?
mcqs.e: The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by 2/3 of members present and voting.

mcqs.q: Parliament's power to legislate on the State List during a National Emergency is in which Article?
mcqs.e: A National Emergency is proclaimed under Article 352.

mcqs.q: Which Article allows Parliament to legislate on the State List at the request of two or more states?
mcqs.e: Such a law applies only to the requesting states and those adopting it.

mcqs.q: Under which Article does Parliament legislate on the State List to implement international treaties?
mcqs.e: Art. 253: international agreements and conventions.

mcqs.q: President's Rule is imposed under which Article?
mcqs.e: National Emergency 352, Financial Emergency 360.

mcqs.q: How long does a law made under Article 250 remain in force?
o: Up to 6 months after the emergency ceases
mcqs.e: It ceases to have effect six months after the emergency ends.

mcqs.q: Which parliamentary committee is a financial committee?
mcqs.e: Three financial committees: Public Accounts, Estimates, Public Undertakings.

mcqs.q: Which are the three financial committees?
o: Public Accounts, Estimates and Public Undertakings Committees
mcqs.e: These are standing committees.

mcqs.q: Members of the Departmentally Related Standing Committees are nominated by whom?
mcqs.e: Standing committees are permanent; ad hoc committees are temporary.

mcqs.q: What is a temporary parliamentary committee called?
mcqs.e: A standing committee functions continuously.

mcqs.q: When was the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) first set up?
mcqs.e: After independence it was first constituted in 1950.

mcqs.q: How many members are there in the Public Accounts Committee?
mcqs.e: Term 1 year; a minister cannot be a member.

mcqs.q: How many members does the Estimates Committee have?
mcqs.e: It is the largest committee, set up in 1950 on John Mathai's recommendation.

mcqs.q: On whose recommendation was the Estimates Committee set up in 1950?
mcqs.e: John Mathai was then the Finance Minister.

mcqs.q: The Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) was set up on whose recommendation?
mcqs.e: It has 22 members (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha).

mcqs.q: Who was the chairman of the First Finance Commission?
mcqs.e: K.C. Neogy headed the First Finance Commission in 1951.

mcqs.q: What is the main purpose of a parliamentary committee?
o: To conduct elections across the country
To examine bills and policies in detail
mcqs.e: Elections are held by the Election Commission; amendments are made by Parliament.

mcqs.q: The Delimitation Commission is constituted under which Article?
mcqs.e: After each census Parliament enacts a Delimitation Act and a commission is set up.

mcqs.q: In which years have Delimitation Commission Acts been enacted?
mcqs.e: Four commissions have been set up.

mcqs.q: Which amendment froze delimitation until 2000?
mcqs.e: Seats were frozen on the basis of the 1971 Census.

mcqs.q: Which amendment extended the freeze on delimitation until 2026?
mcqs.e: The freeze lasts until the first census after 2026.

mcqs.q: Internal readjustment of constituencies on the basis of the 2001 Census was made possible by which amendment?
mcqs.e: The number of seats was unchanged; only boundaries changed.

mcqs.q: To whom has the Constitution given the power to define the powers and privileges of MPs?
mcqs.e: Art. 105(3) lets Parliament define them by law.

mcqs.q: How many chapters are there in Part VI of the Constitution?
mcqs.e: Part VI deals with the States.

mcqs.q: What is the range of Articles in Part VI (The States)?
mcqs.e: Article 152 defines 'State'.

mcqs.q: What is defined in Chapter I of Part VI?
mcqs.e: 'State' has a different meaning in Parts III and IV.

mcqs.q: The State Legislature is described in which Articles?
mcqs.e: Art. 213 deals with the Governor's ordinances.

mcqs.q: The Governor's power to promulgate ordinances is in which Article?
mcqs.e: Formula: add 90 to the President's Article (123 + 90).

mcqs.q: High Courts are described in which Articles?
mcqs.e: Part VI, Chapter V.

mcqs.q: Subordinate courts are described in which Articles?
mcqs.e: Part VI, Chapter VI.

mcqs.q: Why is there no CAG-like post at the state level?
o: The Finance Commission does its work
There is no separate CAG for states at all
mcqs.e: The last chapter of Part V is on the CAG; Part VI has no counterpart.

mcqs.q: Who generally makes laws on police, public health and agriculture?
mcqs.e: These are State List subjects.

mcqs.q: What is the maximum strength of a State Legislative Assembly?
mcqs.e: Assembly: maximum 500, minimum 60 (Lok Sabha maximum 550 under Art. 81).

mcqs.q: What is the minimum strength of a State Legislative Assembly?
mcqs.e: Exceptions: Sikkim 32, Goa 40, Mizoram 40 (Puducherry UT 30).

mcqs.q: Which of the following states has fewer than 60 seats in its Legislative Assembly?
mcqs.e: Goa 40, Mizoram 40, Sikkim 32; Arunachal, Meghalaya, Nagaland have 60.

mcqs.q: How many seats are there in the Sikkim Legislative Assembly?
mcqs.e: Some small states are exempt from the minimum of 60.

mcqs.q: What is the minimum strength of a State Legislative Council?
mcqs.e: Legislative Council: minimum 40, maximum one-third of the Assembly's strength.

mcqs.q: Which Union Territories have Legislative Assemblies?
o: Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir
mcqs.e: Delhi got its Assembly under Art. 239AA.

mcqs.q: Which amendment designated Delhi as the National Capital Territory (NCT)?
mcqs.e: It inserted Article 239AA.

mcqs.q: The Legislative Assembly of Delhi is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Inserted by the 69th Amendment.

mcqs.q: The Union Territory of Goa, Daman and Diu was formed by which amendment?
Puducherry was made a Union Territory by which amendment?
mcqs.e: It was acquired from French control.

mcqs.q: Dadra and Nagar Haveli became a Union Territory of India by which amendment?
By which amendment/year did Goa attain full statehood (as per the lecture)?
mcqs.e: Goa became the 25th state in 1987.

mcqs.q: What types of State Legislatures can exist in India?
mcqs.e: Either an Assembly alone, or an Assembly with a Legislative Council.

mcqs.q: How many states in India have a bicameral legislature?
mcqs.e: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Which of the following states has a Legislative Council?
mcqs.e: Only six states have a Legislative Council.

mcqs.q: Which of the following states does NOT have a Legislative Council?
mcqs.e: Tamil Nadu has a unicameral legislature.

mcqs.q: The State Legislative Council is considered equivalent to which House?
mcqs.e: The Council is the upper house; the Assembly corresponds to the Lok Sabha.

mcqs.q: What is the normal term of a Legislative Assembly?
mcqs.e: During a National Emergency it can be extended by 1 year at a time.

mcqs.q: Within what time after an emergency ends must elections be held?
mcqs.e: An extended term cannot continue beyond 6 months after the emergency ceases.

mcqs.q: Which amendment raised the Lok Sabha's term from 5 to 6 years, and which restored it to 5?
mcqs.e: The 42nd Amendment was passed during Indira Gandhi's tenure.

mcqs.q: What is the English name of the Vidhan Sabha?
mcqs.e: The Vidhan Parishad is called the Legislative Council.

mcqs.q: What is a feature of the State Legislative Council?
o: It is dissolved like the Assembly
It is a permanent House and is not dissolved
mcqs.e: One-third of members retire every 2 years.

mcqs.q: How are members of the Legislative Council elected?
mcqs.e: By proportional representation through single transferable vote.

mcqs.q: What proportion of Legislative Council members retire every 2 years?
mcqs.e: Members serve a 6-year term.

mcqs.q: The composition of the Legislative Assembly is provided in which Article?
The composition of the Legislative Council is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 169 creation/abolition, 170 Assembly, 171 Legislative Council.

mcqs.q: What is the maximum strength of a Legislative Council?
mcqs.e: Raised from 1/4 to 1/3 by the 7th Amendment.

mcqs.q: What change did the 7th Amendment make in Article 171(1)?
o: Raised the maximum limit from 1/4 to 1/3
mcqs.e: The 7th Amendment was enacted in 1956.

mcqs.q: What proportion of Legislative Council members is elected by MLAs?
mcqs.e: 1/3 by local bodies, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, 1/6 nominated by the Governor.

mcqs.q: What proportion of Legislative Council members does the Governor nominate?
mcqs.e: From literature, science, art, co-operative movement and social service.

mcqs.q: What is the minimum qualification for graduate electors of a Legislative Council?
mcqs.e: Teacher electors also need at least 3 years of teaching experience.

mcqs.q: Besides literature, science, art and social service, the Governor's nominees to the Legislative Council may have special knowledge of which field?
mcqs.e: Art. 171(5) lists literature, science, art, co-operative movement and social service.

mcqs.q: The 97th Amendment gave constitutional status to which subject?
mcqs.e: It inserted Part IXB.

mcqs.q: Which Articles of Part IXB relate to co-operative societies?
mcqs.e: Art. 43B was also added to the Directive Principles.

mcqs.q: The oath of newly elected members of a State Legislature is in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 99 for Parliament; for states 99 + 89 = 188.

mcqs.q: Roughly what number must be added to a Parliament Article to get the State Legislature Article (lecture formula)?
Summoning, prorogation of the State Legislature and dissolution of the Assembly are provided in which Article?
The Governor's special address is in which Article?
Disqualification of State Legislature members is in which Article?
Which Article relates to the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council?
mcqs.e: 182 = 93 + 89; Assembly Speaker is Art. 178.

mcqs.q: Which Article relates to the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly?
mcqs.e: In states the Assembly comes first, then the Council; in Parliament the order is reversed.

mcqs.q: Who elects the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly?
mcqs.e: They choose the Speaker and Deputy Speaker from among themselves.

mcqs.q: How is the Chairman of a Legislative Council chosen?
o: Elected by Council members from among themselves
mcqs.e: In the Rajya Sabha, the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman.

mcqs.q: Who vote in the election of the Vice-President?
o: All members of both Houses of Parliament (elected and nominated)
mcqs.e: The Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.q: Who is the current Vice-President (as per the lecture)?
mcqs.e: He is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.q: Who is the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (as per the lecture)?
mcqs.e: The Deputy Chairman is elected by Rajya Sabha members.

mcqs.q: Who is the current Speaker of the Lok Sabha (as per the lecture)?
mcqs.e: He was re-elected Speaker in the 18th Lok Sabha.

mcqs.q: Under the RPA 1951, what qualification is needed to become a member of a State Legislature?
o: Being registered as an elector in an assembly constituency of that state
mcqs.e: For the Rajya Sabha, the domicile condition was removed in 2003.

mcqs.q: When was the requirement of being an elector of the concerned state removed for the Rajya Sabha?
mcqs.e: For example, Manmohan Singh was a Rajya Sabha member from Assam.

mcqs.q: What is the minimum age to become a member of a Legislative Assembly?
mcqs.e: 30 years for a Legislative Council member.

mcqs.q: What is the minimum age to become a member of a Legislative Council?
mcqs.e: Same as for the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.q: The Annual Financial Statement (Budget) of a state is in which Article?
mcqs.e: 112 + 90 = 202; it is laid in the name of the Governor.

mcqs.q: In whose name is the State Budget laid?
mcqs.e: The Finance Minister presents it.

mcqs.q: Which of the following financial powers does the Governor NOT have?
o: Levying taxes independently without legislative approval
Causing the Budget to be laid before the legislature
mcqs.e: Taxes can be levied only with legislative approval.

mcqs.q: Who administers the Contingency Fund of a state?
mcqs.e: The Contingency Fund of India is at the disposal of the President (Art. 267).

mcqs.q: Who appoints the Chief Minister?
mcqs.e: The Council of Ministers headed by the CM is collectively responsible to the Assembly.

mcqs.q: To whom is the State Council of Ministers collectively responsible?
mcqs.e: Article 164(2).

mcqs.q: On whose advice does the Governor dissolve the Legislative Assembly?
o: The Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister
mcqs.e: The Governor acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

mcqs.q: Is there a provision for joint sittings in State Legislatures?
o: No, there is no joint sitting in State Legislatures
mcqs.e: In a deadlock the Council can only delay a bill.

mcqs.q: When can an ordinance be promulgated?
o: When at least one House of the legislature is not in session
When both Houses are in session
mcqs.e: An ordinance must be approved within 6 weeks of reassembly.

mcqs.q: Within how long after reassembly must an ordinance be approved by the legislature?
mcqs.e: Otherwise it lapses automatically.

mcqs.q: In which case was repeated re-promulgation of ordinances called a 'fraud on the Constitution'?
o: D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar
mcqs.e: The Governor of Bihar had repeatedly re-promulgated ordinances.

mcqs.q: On which subjects can the President/Governor promulgate ordinances?
o: Subjects on which Parliament/State Legislature can make laws
mcqs.e: Ordinance power is co-extensive with the legislature's law-making power.

mcqs.q: Privileges of State Legislature members are in which Article?
A bill becomes an Act only when it is passed by whom?
o: Passed by both Houses and assented to
mcqs.e: Since both Houses are needed, an ordinance can be issued when even one House is not in session.

mcqs.q: Who decides questions of disqualification of State Legislature members (Art. 192)?
o: Governor (on the opinion of the Election Commission)
mcqs.e: Like Art. 103 for Parliament; Art. 192 for states.
